title: Dual-State Parallel Fields (Half-Migrated State Tracking)
pattern: Maintaining both a raw, type-unsafe primitive representation of a state/field and its strongly-typed counterpart side-by-side inside the same object, with setters syncing them to avoid updating old callers.
why_bad: Violation of the Single Source of Truth invariant. Storing the same state in two different formats inside the same struct inevitably leads to synchronization bugs when one field is updated but the other is missed. It bypasses type-safety and forces code to compile with redundant, error-prone data structures.
detection:
The linter must observe:
1. Two struct fields tracking the same concept in different formats (e.g., `String` and `Enum`).
2. Mutator functions maintaining double writes to ensure synchrony between them.
